support_sara: FYI escalation from SE — customer hit repeated partial streaming responses after auth rotation + reconnect. They see missing final frame and duplicate billing sometimes. Repro attached. :eyes:
ryan_eng: ack, can you paste the repro steps and any server logs?
maya_devx: also which SDK — python, node, ts, go? that changes iterator behavior.
support_sara: internal notes from customer: using our hosted API via SSE. Token rotates every 60s. Sequence: initial stream starts, token rotates, client reconnects with new token -> receives a partial payload (missing final 'event: done' / final chunk) and the SDK iterator resolves without last text. Customer reported duplicate bill for that call in ~12% of reconnects. Repro commands below.
support_sara: curl repro (simplified):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=text-6"
# rotate token externally, then reconnect immediately
```
support_sara: Node repro (EventSource):
```js
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('chunk', e.data);
// on reconnect we see final chunk missing
```
support_sara: Python repro (aiohttp async iterator):
```py
async with session.get(url, headers={'Authorization': token}) as r:
    async for line in r.content:
        process(line)
# iterator exits without the last chunk after reconnect
```
ingrid_oncall: logsbot pulled the server-side connection logs: we see the second connection’s request id created, but the final chunk for the previous stream is logged as "queued" and never flushed when reconnect happens rapidly. snippet:
```
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] conn-id=abc123 stream flush queued final-chunk
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] auth-rotate token=rotated for customer_x
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] conn-id=def456 new-conn start
[2026-03-12T14:02:11Z] billing charge event=stream_start conn=def456 amount=0.002
```
billing_john: that could explain duplicate billing — new connection created triggers a new charge before finalizing previous. we charge on stream start. we should consider idempotency via client-provided request-id header. do they provide one?
support_sara: customer does not. they use default ephemeral request ids.
ryan_eng: reproducer for me locally: can trigger by forcing token rotate and immediately opening new SSE. I can see final chunk sits in runtime worker KV cache and is skipped during abrupt handoff. looks like a race between handoff flush and worker rebind.
maya_devx: on client side, some SDKs treat eventsource closing as terminal and resolve the iterator — but if the server hadn't sent a double-newline terminator, the client might not get last piece. we need defensive behavior both sides.
ryan_eng: propose action items:
- runtime: ensure handoff path flushes outstanding final frames synchronously before accepting new connection for same session / request-id (ENG-RUNTIME)
- api: accept optional X-Redwood-Request-Id header and use it to dedupe billing events (BILLING)
- devex: add SDK retry/merge logic to buffer until final delimiter or short grace period before resolving iterator (DEVEX)
- add regression tests for rapid auth rotation + reconnect (QA)
maya_devx: temporary workaround we can recommend to customer: include a stable X-Redwood-Request-Id per logical request and add a 200-300ms jitter before reconnect to allow flush. also upgrade to latest TS SDK which has a small buffering window.
ingrid_oncall: assigning to ryan_eng for runtime triage and to billing_john for dedupe discussion. I also flagged infra for a short-term metric that counts mid-handshake reconnects so we can measure frequency. :hammer_and_wrench:
ryan_eng: starting a repro branch now. initial finding: when token rotates, auth middleware immediately closes old socket; handoff was relying on asynchronous flush which loses final frames on preemptive close. fix is to block close until flush completes or send an explicit "handoff:pending" event to client. I'll open PR with tests.
support_sara: thanks — can we keep the customer updated? they're very sensitive because this impacts billing and UX.
ryan_eng: will post updates here. ETA for tentative fix branch + integration test: 48h.
billing_john: I'll prototype dedupe logic; if request-id present, only bill first stream_start per id and mark subsequent stream_start as reattach. if not present, we can consider a short TTL cache keyed by client ip + model + user to reduce duplicates (short-term).
maya_devx: once runtime patch lands, we'll push a tiny patch to the python/ts SDKs to wait for final delimiter by default and expose option to opt out.
logsbot: recorded thread and uploaded server logs to internal bucket: s3://redwood-debug/esc-1768504321/ (link shared to eng channel)
deploy-bot: scheduled canary for runtime patch against staging after tests pass.
ryan_eng: reproducer notes for test harness: simulate token rotation by sending auth-change event, then immediately initiate new SSE. verify final chunk content equality and that billing events count == 1 when request-id header present.
support_sara: perfect. tagging @maya_devx @billing_john @ingrid_oncall for follow up. :white_check_mark:
